ActionChanging_helpMark:
Controls whether Actions on your Hotbar will be Replaced with combos from the plugin.
If disabled, your manual presses of abilities will no longer be affected by any Wrath settings.

Auto-Rotation will work regardless of the setting.
ActionChanging_recommendedValue: On (This is essentially turning OFF most of Wrath)
ActionChanging_warningMark:
Wrath is largely designed with Action Replacing in mind.
Only Auto-Rotation will work if this is disabled.
Disabling it may also lead to unexpected behavior, such as regarding Retargeting.
AddOutOfPartyNPCsToRetargeting_helpMark:
This will add any NPCs that are not in your party to the retargeting logic for healing actions.

Useful for healers who want to be able to target NPCs that are not in their party, such as quest NPCs.
These NPCs will not generally work with any role-based custom Heal Stack entries
(even if an NPC looks like a tank, they're not always classified as one)
AddOutOfPartyNPCsToRetargeting_recommend: On (If you use Retargeting at all)
AoEDamageTTS_helpMark: Will play a text-to-speech sound clip whenever a stack/group damage cast is detected, including who it is targeting if applicable.
AoEDamageToast_helpMark: Show a message on-screen whenever a stack/group damage cast is detected, including who it is targeting if applicable.
AprilFools2026_defaultValue: On, cause it's that type of day y'know
AprilFools2026_helpMark: For when you can't get enough MNK in your plugin.
AprilFools2026_recommendedValue: Off, unless your name starts with Beep
BlockSpellOnMove_helpMark:
Will completely block actions while moving.
This would supersede combo-specific movement options, which many jobs have.
BlockSpellOnMove_recommendedValue: Off (Most Jobs will handle this better with their Features)
CustomHealStack_helpMark:
If there are fewer than 4 items, and all return nothing when checked, will fall back to Self.

These targets will only be considered valid if they are friendly and within 25y.

When applied to something like Esuna, these targets will be checked for having a Cleansable Debuff, etc.
So adding 'Any Cleansable Ally' or similar is not necessary.
EnabledOutputLog_helpMark: Will print to chat every time you use an action provided by Wrath.
EnabledOutputLog_recommendedValue: On (IF trying to report an issue)
HideChildren_helpMark: Will hide the Features and Options under disabled Combos.
HideConflictedCombos_helpMark: Will hide Combos that conflict with Combos that you have enabled.
HideMessageOfTheDay_helpMark: Will prevent the Message of the Day from being shown in your chat upon login.
InterruptDelay_helpMark:
Controls the percentage of a total cast time to wait before interrupting enemy casts.
Applies to all interrupts (including stuns used to interrupt) in every Job's Combos.
InterruptDelay_recommendedValue: below 40 (Above that and you start failing to interrupt many short casts)
MaximumWeavesPerWindow_helpMark:
Controls how many oGCDs are allowed between GCDs.
The 'default' for the game is double weaving, but triple weaving is completely possible with low enough latency (of every kind);but if you struggle with latency of any sort then single weaving may even be a good answer to try for you.
Triple weaving is already done in a manner where we try to avoid clipping GCDs, and as such doesn't happen particularly often even if you have good latency, and is a valid thing to do, so it is a safe option if you want.
MeleeOffset_helpMark:
Controls what is considered to be in melee range.
Mainly for those who don't want to switch to ranged attacks if the boss walks slightly outside of range.
For example a value of -0.5 would make you have to be 0.5 yalms closer to the target,
or a value of 2 would allow you to be 2 yalms further away and still be considered in melee range
(melee actions wouldn't work, but it would give you some warning instead of just suddenly doing less optimal actions).
MovementLeeway_helpMark:
This controls how long of a delay is needed before Wrath recognizes you as moving.
This allows you to not have to worry about small movements affecting your rotation, primarily for casters.
MovementLeeway_recommendedValue: 0.0-1.0 (Above that gets into the territory of breaking any Movement Options in your Job)
OpenToCurrentJobOnSwitch_Name: Open PvE Features Tab to Current Job on Switching Jobs
OpenToCurrentJobOnSwitch_helpMark: Will automatically switch the PvE Features tab to the job you are currently playing, when you switch jobs.
OpenToCurrentJob_Name: Open PvE Features Tab to Current Job on Opening
OpenToCurrentJob_helpMark: When the PvE Features tab is opened it will automatically open to your current Job.
OpenToPvE_Name: Open Wrath to the PvE Features Tab
OpenToPvE_helpMark:
When you open Wrath with `/wrath`, it will open to the PvE Features tab, instead of the last tab you were on.
Same as always using the `/wrath pve` command to open Wrath.
OpenToPvP_Name: Open Wrath to the PvP Features Tab in PvP areas
OpenToPvP_helpMark:
Same as above, when you open Wrath with `/wrath`, it will open to the PvP Features tab, instead of the last tab you were on, when in a PvP area.
Similar to using the `/wrath pvp` command to open Wrath.
OpenerTimeout_helpMark:
Controls how long of a gap with no action is allowed in an Opener, before it is considered failed and normal rotation is resumed.
Can be necessary for some casters to increase, particularly when the first action of an Opener is a hard-cast.
OutputOpenerLogs_helpMark:
Will print the status of your Job's Opener to chat.
e.g. When it is Ready, Fails, or Finishes.
OutputOpenerLogs_recommendedValue: On (IF trying to troubleshoot an Opener)
OverwriteQueue_helpMark: This will allow you to overwrite whatever is currently queued up with another action.
PenaltyPause_helpMark:
Will lockout combos on your hotbar when detected mechanics that inflict a penalty for using an action is detected (e.g pyretics, acceleration bombs, gazes etc.) has this much time left before resolving.

Some mechanics may override this value.

Set to 0 to disable.
PenaltyPause_recommendedValue: Increase with higher latency to the server
QueueAdjustThreshold_helpMark: Will allow you to queue when the GCD is at this time or less.
QueueAdjustThreshold_warningMark: Setting this too low or to zero will make it really hard to manually queue.
QueueAdjust_helpMark: Allows you to adjust your queue window to any time during the GCD rather than just within the last 0.3-0.5s. Useful if you're not mashing the key or using Auto-Rotation and wish to manually intervene.
RaiseStack_defaultValue: Any Healer > Any Tank > Any Raiser > Any Dead Party Member
RaiseStack_helpMark:
This is the order in which Wrath will try to select a target to Raise,
if Retargeting of any Raise Feature is enabled.

You can find Raise Features under PvE>General,
or under each caster that has a Raise.

If there are fewer than 5 items, and all return nothing when checked, will fall back to:
your Hard Target if they're dead, or <Any Dead Party Member>.

These targets will only be considered valid if they are friendly, dead, and within 30y.
RetargetHealingActionsToStack_helpMark:
Will Retarget all Single-Target Healing Actions to the Heal Stack as shown below,
similarly to how Redirect or Reaction would.
This ensures that the target used to check HP% threshold logic for healing actions is the same target that will receive that heal.
RetargetHealingActionsToStack_recommende: On (If you customize the Heal Stack AT ALL)
ShortDTRText_helpMark:
Will hide the number of active Auto-Mode Combos.
By default the Server Info Bar shows:
- Whether Auto-Rotation is on or off
- (if on) The number of active Auto-Mode Combos
- (if applicable) Whether another plugin is controlling the state of Auto-Rotation.
ShowBorderAroundOptionsWithChildren_Name: Show Borders around Combos and Features with Options
ShowBorderAroundOptionsWithChildren_help: Will draw a border around Combos and Features that have Features and Options of their own.
ShowOpenerDtr_Name: Opener Status in Server Info Bar
ShowOpenerDtr_helpMark: Shows the status of your current opener, if enabled and applicable.
ShowTargetHighlight_extraText: (Only used by AST and DNC currently)
ShowTargetHighlight_helpMark: Draws a box around party members in the vanilla Party List, when targeted by certain Features.
SuppressAutorotCommand_helpMark: Will hide chat feedback for /wrath auto commands
SuppressSetCommands_Name: Suppress Set and Unset commands feedback
SuppressSetCommands_helpMark:
Will hide chat feedback for /wrath set and /wrath unset commands.
(Will still show feedback if the command is being overriden by IPC, or fails)
TankbusterTTS_helpMark: Will play a text-to-speech sound clip whenever a tankbuster is detected, including who it is targeting.
TankbusterToast_helpMark: Show a message on-screen whenever a tankbuster is detected, including who it is targeting.
TargetHighlightColor_helpMark: Controls the color of the box drawn around party members.
Throttle_helpMark:
Will restrict how often Combos will update the Action on your Hotbar.
At 50ms it's not really restrictive, always giving you an up to date action.

If you are looking for some (fairly minor) FPS gains then you can increase this value to make Combos run less often.
This makes your combos less responsive, and perhaps even clips GCDs.
At high values this will clip your GCDs by several seconds or break your rotation altogether.
UIShowPresetIDs_Name: Show Preset IDs next to Combo Names
UIShowPresetIDs_helpMark:
Displays the Preset ID number next to the name of each Combo and Feature.
These are the IDs used for commands like `/wrath toggle <ID>`.
Pre-7.3 the behavior was to show a number here, but it was much shorter, and did not work in commands.
UIShowSearchBar_helpMark: Controls whether Search Bars should be shown in Settings, and PvE and PvP Jobs.
UseCustomHealStack_Name: Use a Custom Heal Stack Instead
UseCustomHealStack_helpMark:
Select this if you would rather make your own stack of target priorities for Heal Targets instead of using our default stack.

It is recommended to use this to align with your Redirect/Reaction configuration IF you're not using the Retarget Healing Actions option above; otherwise it is preference.
UseExperimentalHP_helpMark:
This is a new way of evaluating current HP values, using pre-emptively obtained values to update health values internally before it is reflected in-game properly.

As such, you may see things happen earlier than what may be expected, as values for damage and healing are generated much earlier than shown in game. For example, as soon as you hit the slidecast window the value of the spell is already known.

This is actually best recommended for healers using auto-rotation to mitigate the amount of double casted heals. For DPS, this will switch targets with auto-rotation the moment a killing blow goes out, rather than waiting until the target is officially recognized as dead.

Used currently when evaluating HP% checks in features and auto-rotation.
UseExperimentalHP_warningMark: This is highly experimental, and may have undesired behaviours. Please be vigilant and report this.
UseFieldMouseoverOverridesInDefaultHealS: Add Field MouseOver to the Default Healing Stack

Will add any MouseOver targets to the top of the Default Heal Stack, overriding the rest of the stack if you are mousing over any party member UI.

It is recommended to enable this if you are a keyboard+mouse user and enable Retarget Healing Actions (or have UI MouseOver targets in your Redirect/Reaction configuration).
UseFocusTargetOverrideInDefaultHealStack: Add Focus Target to the Default Healing Stack
This will add your focus target under your hard and soft targets in the Default Heal Stack, overriding the rest of the stack if you have a living focus target.
UseLowestHPOverrideInDefaultHealStack_Na: Add Lowest HP% Ally to the Default Healing Stack
UseLowestHPOverrideInDefaultHealStack_he: This will add a nearby party member with the lowest HP% to bottom of the Default Heal Stack, overriding only yourself.
UseLowestHPOverrideInDefaultHealStack_wa:
Unlike the other Default+ Options, this one is not an option in most other Retargeting Plugins.
THIS SHOULD BE USED WITH THE 'RETARGET HEALING ACTIONS' SETTING ABOVE!
UseUIMouseoverOverridesInDefaultHealStac: Add UI MouseOver to the Default Healing Stack

Will add any UI MouseOver targets to the top of the Default Heal Stack, overriding the rest of the stack if you are mousing over any party member UI.

It is recommended to enable this if you are a keyboard+mouse user and enable Retarget Healing Actions (or have UI MouseOver targets in your Redirect/Reaction configuration).
